prompt:
# Subject Merge Fine Clustering

## Quick Start

Inside one topic area, create tight candidate clusters that are worth a later same-concept decision. Use only the provided candidate cards.

## Identity Filter

Cluster candidates only when they might be the same teachable idea at the same level, testable with the same question.

Do not cluster just because candidates share a keyword. Keep candidates separate when one adds implementation, math, limitation, application, deeper mechanism, tool-specific behavior, or a broader/narrower student action.

Doubt means singleton. Under-clustering is safer than sending unrelated candidates to merge evaluation.

## Output

Return one JSON object only:

```json
{
  "clusters": [
    {
      "id": "cluster_001",
      "label": "Short candidate cluster",
      "rationale": "Why these candidates may share concept identity.",
      "candidate_ids": ["candidate-id"]
    }
  ]
}
```

## Self-Check

- Every input candidate ID appears exactly once.
- Each non-singleton cluster has a plausible same-concept reason.
- Implementation, limitation, application, math, and deeper-revisit candidates were not grouped with definitions just because labels overlap.
- Mixed-language same-level candidates were clustered when their teachable idea matches.
- No web search or external knowledge was used.

area.label: NLP Foundations and Definitions
area.rationale: Covers introductory definitions of NLP, its everyday applications, and basic concepts that frame the field.

candidates.label: Natural Language Processing (NLP) Definition
candidates.description: NLP is a branch of AI that enables machines to read, understand, and derive meaning from human languages, combining linguistics and computer science.
coverage_criteria: Define NLP and its two foundational fields: linguistics and computer science.
candidates.lesson_title: Introdução ao Processamento de Linguagem Natural

candidates.label: Everyday Applications of NLP
candidates.description: Common NLP applications include autocorrect for spelling and plagiarism checkers that scan for duplicate content.
coverage_criteria: List and describe two everyday NLP applications, such as autocorrect and plagiarism checking.
candidates.lesson_title: Introdução ao Processamento de Linguagem Natural

candidates.label: Word Normalization: Stemming and Lemmatization
candidates.description: Stemming reduces words to root forms by cutting suffixes (e.g., 'skipping' → 'skip'), while lemmatization uses dictionary-based analysis to find base forms (e.g., 'am', 'are', 'is' → 'be').
coverage_criteria: Define stemming and lemmatization, and contrast one with the other with examples.
candidates.lesson_title: Introdução ao Processamento de Linguagem Natural

candidates.label: Linguistic Annotation: POS Tagging and Named Entity Recognition
candidates.description: POS tagging labels words with grammatical categories (noun, verb, etc.), while Named Entity Recognition identifies names, locations, and organizations in text.
coverage_criteria: Explain what POS tagging and Named Entity Recognition are, giving examples of each.
candidates.lesson_title: Introdução ao Processamento de Linguagem Natural

candidates.label: Machine Learning in NLP
candidates.description: After preprocessing, ML algorithms like Naive Bayes can be applied to tasks such as sentiment analysis, learning patterns from labeled data.
coverage_criteria: Describe the role of machine learning in NLP, giving Naive Bayes as an example.
candidates.lesson_title: Introdução ao Processamento de Linguagem Natural

candidates.label: NLP Definition and Suitability Criteria
candidates.description: Natural Language Processing (NLP) is a branch of artificial intelligence that uses machine learning to process and interpret texts and data. Three characteristics indicate when NLP is appropriate: the need to understand human communication, the requirement for the machine to respond with precision, and the ability to process and analyze large volumes of data for predictions or suggestions.
coverage_criteria: Define NLP as presented in the lesson.
List the three characteristics that make NLP suitable for problem-solving.
Give an example of a problem that would benefit from these characteristics.
candidates.lesson_title: Processamento de texto, métricas e técnicas

candidates.label: Aplicações de PLN (Visão Geral)
candidates.description: Lista e descreve aplicações de PLN: informação, tradução automática, sistemas de recomendação, smart replies, reconhecimento de voz, análise de sentimento, Q&A, extração de informação, sumarização, classificação, modelagem de tópicos, OCR, NER e geração de linguagem natural.
coverage_criteria: Citar pelo menos cinco aplicações de PLN.
Escolher uma aplicação e explicar como o PLN é usado.
candidates.lesson_title: Processamento de texto, métricas e técnicas

candidates.label: Desafios do PLN: Segmentação, Contexto e Semântica
candidates.description: Aborda desafios fundamentais do PLN: segmentação de texto, análise de contexto, extração de significado semântico e ambiguidade.
coverage_criteria: Explicar o desafio da segmentação em PLN com um exemplo.
Descrever como a ambiguidade pode dificultar a interpretação de frases.
candidates.lesson_title: Processamento de texto, métricas e técnicas

candidates.label: Why Text Needs to Be Converted to Numbers for Machine Learning
candidates.description: Machine learning algorithms require numerical input (matrices). Text data must be vectorized into feature vectors so that models can learn a mapping Y=f(X).
coverage_criteria: Explain the necessity of numerical representation for ML models.
Describe the Y=f(X) formulation and the role of vectorization.
candidates.lesson_title: Representação de palavras e "Bag of Words" (BoW)

candidates.label: Natural Language Challenges
candidates.description: Natural language is inherently structured yet free-form; the same meaning can be expressed in many ways, and similar words can convey different meanings, making NLP distinct from other data types.
coverage_criteria: Give examples of sentences where similar words convey different meanings, and explain why NLP requires special approaches compared to tabular data.
candidates.lesson_title: Representação de palavras e "Bag of Words" (BoW)

candidates.label: Introduction to Natural Language Processing (NLP)
candidates.description: NLP is the field of making computers understand natural language, relying on statistical approximations; applications include information extraction and chatbots.
coverage_criteria: Explain that NLP deals with understanding natural language by machines.
Mention that approaches are statistical and approximate.
Give examples of applications such as document information extraction or chatbots.
candidates.lesson_title: Biblioteca de manipulação de texto: NLTK e Spacy

candidates.label: Natural Language Processing (NLP) Definition
candidates.description: NLP is a subfield of AI focused on enabling computers to process and analyze human language, applied to tasks like text classification and sentiment analysis.
coverage_criteria: Define NLP.
Give an example of an NLP task.
candidates.lesson_title: NLTK, BoW e Naive Bayes para Análise de Conteúdo

candidates.label: Rede Neural Artificial
candidates.description: Uma rede neural artificial é um modelo preditivo inspirado no cérebro, composto por neurônios artificiais conectados que realizam cálculos ponderados sobre as entradas e produzem saídas através de funções de ativação.
coverage_criteria: Definir o que é uma rede neural artificial e seus componentes principais (neurônios, conexões, função de ativação).
Descrever como um neurônio artificial calcula sua saída a partir das entradas, pesos e função de ativação.

candidate_assignment_rule: Cluster only. Every input candidate ID must appear exactly once across clusters. Prefer tight clusters; topic overlap alone is not a cluster.

web_access_policy.instruction: Do not use web search or open URLs. Use only the provided candidate cards.
